parakeet-tdt-ctc-110m/long: On a quiet morning the harbour was still, the fishing boats rested against the pier, and the gulls waited on the posts for the first catch of the day. Maria walked along the water with a notebook in her hand. She had come to the coast to write about the lighthouse, which had guided ships past the rocks for more than two hundred years. The keeper, an old man named Thomas, met her at the gate. He told her that the lamp had been electric since nineteen fifty, but that he still climbed the stairs every evening to check the lens. There are one hundred and twelve steps, he said, and I have counted them every night for thirty one years. From the top they could see the whole bay, the green hills behind the town, and a container ship moving slowly toward the open sea. Maria asked him whether he ever felt lonely. Thomas laughed and said that the sea was never the same twice, and that a person who watches it carefully always has company. Before she left, he showed her the logbook where every storm, every fog and every passing ship had been written down in careful handwriting. She photographed a page from the winter of nineteen eighty seven, when the wind had broken three windows and the power had failed for two days. That night, back at the hotel, she began her article with the sound of the waves and the steady light turning over the water.
